title: GPU matrix multiplication (single precision)
short_description: Large single precision matrix multiplication through the vendor's own maths library.

structured_text.description: Multiplies a pair of large single precision matrices on the graphics processor, using the maths library the hardware vendor ships for exactly this job and the fastest single precision path that library offers. The matrices are sized to fill a meaningful share of graphics memory, so the result depends on the whole stack: the arithmetic units, the memory hierarchy that feeds them, and the quality of the vendor's own software.
structured_text.metric_explanation: Throughput is the number of single precision operations per second during the multiply, in billions, reported in GFLOPS.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Higher is better. This is the figure that best predicts dense linear algebra work in engineering and scientific codes, which is dominated by matrix multiplication at this scale.
structured_text.reasoning: Single precision dense linear algebra is the backbone of simulation, engineering and classical scientific computing. Modern hardware reaches it through reduced precision paths inside the vendor library, so the delivered rate can differ greatly from the raw single precision figure, and only running the real library shows which.
